f47726c8de464ea1.description:
Company: Spacewire Tech
Location: HSR Layout, Bengaluru (Work From Office)
Experience: 6 months to 2 years. (NO REMOTE/WFH)

About us
We build subscription apps for Bharat: the hundreds of millions of people in tier 2, 3 and 4 India who pay by UPI and live on their phones. Our apps include BhaktiLok (daily devotion, aartis, AI palm and face reading), MeraTune (ringtones with your own name in them), CashAlert (voice alerts for UPI payments) and HeyBuddy (voice lock and assistant).
We are a small team that ships fast. An idea on Monday is usually a live test by Friday, and the numbers decide who was right.
The role
You will own the path from install to paid subscriber on one or more of our apps: onboarding, paywall, trial, autopay and retention. You work directly with the founders, engineers, designers and the ads team, and you get real ownership from week one — this is a backfill role, so you'll be stepping into live funnels and running experiments from day one, not easing in slowly.
This is a junior role (6 months to 2 years of experience). We care more about how you think and how fast you learn than about your title so far.
What you'll do
• Run experiments on onboarding, paywalls, pricing and trials, from hypothesis to result, and call the winner with data.
• Live in Mixpanel: build funnels, spot where users drop, and turn that into the next test.
• Track the subscription numbers that matter: login to trial, trial to paid, autopay success, renewals and churn.
• Write short, clear PRDs and work with engineers and designers to ship them quickly.
• Tear down competitor apps and bring back what is worth testing.
• Work with the ads team so the promise in the ad matches the first screen of the app.
• Shape features around how our users actually behave: regional languages, low-end Android phones, UPI autopay habits.
• Use AI tools every day to move faster on research, specs, copy and analysis.
Who we're looking for
You should have
• A feel for consumer apps in India, especially subscription, UPI autopay or content apps for the next billion users.
• Comfort with numbers. You can read a funnel, question it, and explain what it means in two lines.
• Clear writing in English and good spoken Hindi. You should be able to think like a user in Patna as easily as one in Pune.
• A bias to ship. You would rather run a rough test this week than a perfect one next month.
• Curiosity. You install apps just to see how their paywall works.
Good to have
• Hands-on time with Mixpanel, Firebase or a similar analytics tool.
• Hands-on experience with UPI AutoPay, mandate flows, recurring billing, or payment retry/dunning logic — big plus given our autopay and D2C payments work.
• Exposure to paywalls, pricing tests, payment gateways (Razorpay, Juspay, etc.) or Meta ads.
• Experience in devotional, astrology, utility or entertainment apps.
• A side project, app, page or channel you grew yourself.
Why you'll like it here
Real ownership. Your tests go live to real users, and you see the result in days.
Grow with us. This is an immediate backfill with real scope from day one — if you own it well, there's a clear path from Associate PM to PM as the product and team grow.
Learn the full stack of a subscription business. Product, pricing, payments, ads and analytics, all in one seat.
The gear you need. Laptop, tools, AI subscriptions: ask and it is sorted.
We celebrate. Team parties every month, and nobody needs a reason.
No heavy process. Few meetings, short docs, quick decisions.
A fun bunch. We take the numbers seriously and ourselves a lot less.
How to apply
Send your resume to [email to add] with two things:
• One app you think has a great paywall or onboarding, and why.
• One thing you would test first on any of our apps.

Interested applicants can send their resumes to hr@spacewiretech.com / 6363598861

About The Role

We are seeking a highly skilled Senior Java API developer with experience in building high-performing, scalable, enterprise-grade backend systems in the digital advertising domain.

In this role, you will design, develop, and optimize backend services powering Mobile Ad SDK systems and AI-driven products such as recommendation engines, monetization optimization platforms, and intelligent ad delivery systems. This role will be responsible for productionizing machine learning models, building high-performance APIs, and enabling intelligent decision systems at scale

• Own end-to-end solution design, planning, execution, and release of backend features.
• Build and maintain backend services supporting AI-driven initiatives (recommendation systems, predictive analytics). 
• Productionize and integrate ML models into backend systems, enabling real-time intelligent decisioning. 
• Develop efficient data models and optimize database queries (MySQL/PostgreSQL) for performance and reliability. 
• Ensure API security using OAuth2, JWT, and role-based access controls.

We’d Love for You to Have 

• 3–6 years of experience in Java development in Linux/UNIX environments. 
• Strong proficiency in Core Java, OOPS, Data Structures, and J2EE technologies. 
• Hands-on experience with Spring, Spring Boot, and Hibernate. 
• Strong experience in REST Web Services development and microservices architecture. 
• Proficiency in SQL, schema design, indexing, performance tuning, and complex queries. 
• Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, Jenkins, Maven, Git, and CI/CD pipelines. 
• Experience working on high-performance and scalable AdTech systems (preferred). 
• Working knowledge of Python and integration with AI/ML services. 
• Understanding of advanced AI concepts including RAG, agentic AI, model fine-tuning, and recommendation systems. 
• Experience in JUnit, TDD, refactoring, and Agile development practices. 
• Demonstrated ability to work independently and drive technical ownership. 

Qualification

Should have a bachelor’s degree in engineering or an equivalent degree from a well-known institute/university.

Additional Information

Return to Office: PubMatic employees throughout the globe have returned to our offices via a hybrid work schedule (3 days “in office” and 2 days “working remotely”) that is intended to maximize collaboration, innovation, and productivity among teams and across functions.

Benefits: Our benefits package includes the best of what leading organizations provide, such as paternity/maternity leave, healthcare insurance, broadband reimbursement. As well, when we’re back in the office, we all benefit from a kitchen loaded with healthy snacks and drinks and catered lunches and much more!.

Diversity and Inclusion: PubMatic is proud to be an equal opportunity employer; we don’t just value diversity, we promote and celebrate it. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status

About PubMatic

PubMatic is one of the world’s leading scaled digital advertising platforms, offering more transparent advertising solutions to publishers, media buyers, commerce companies and data owners, allowing them to harness the power and potential of the open internet to drive better business outcomes.

Founded in 2006 with the vision that data-driven decisioning would be the future of digital advertising, we enable content creators to run a more profitable advertising business, which in turn allows them to invest back into the multi-screen and multi-format content that consumers demand.

f4d91041f458930e.description: **About BI Connector** BI Connector, by Guidanz Inc., connects Oracle Fusion data (ERP, HCM, SCM and CX) to the tools data teams already use, including Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, Tableau, Snowflake and Databricks. **The role** * Are you an Oracle Fusion data expert who loves the spotlight, enjoys teaching on camera, and wants to be known as the go-to voice for getting Fusion data into the modern data and AI stack? * You will be the public face of BI Connector: an Oracle Fusion subject matter expert who speaks the language of data engineers and BI developers, and shows them how to get to Fusion ERP, SCM and HCM data efficiently. Your main channel is YouTube, through tutorials, product demos and point-of-view videos that help data teams solve real problems. **What's in it for you** * Your name and face, globally. You become a recognised voice for Oracle Fusion data, in front of enterprise data and BI teams in the US, UK, Middle East and India. * A real say in the product. What you hear from viewers and customers shapes the BI Connector roadmap. You work directly with the core team members. * Freedom to have opinions. We want your point of view on data architecture, not scripted marketing. * Ownership. You build the channel from the ground up and own its strategy, standards and results. * A career-defining niche. Few people combine Oracle Fusion, BI and data engineering on camera. This role makes you one of them. **Who you will be speaking to** * Data engineering teams building pipelines and incremental loads into Fabric, Snowflake and Databricks. * BI and reporting teams building Power BI and Tableau models and dashboards for Finance, HR and Supply Chain users. * Both audiences work on non-Oracle stacks. Your job is to speak their language first, then translate Fusion data into it. **What you will do** * Plan, script, present and record one long-form YouTube tutorial or demo per week, and turn each one into Shorts, LinkedIn clips, a blog post and, where useful, a starter kit. * Build and maintain demo environments across Oracle Fusion and destination tools. * Own titles, descriptions, chapters and playlists, and work with a freelance editor and designer on final quality. * Co-present thought leadership videos with our CEO. * Write blog posts, quick-start guides and starter kits such as Power BI templates and Fabric pipeline starters. * Answer Oracle Fusion data questions in the Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, Snowflake, Reddit, Stack Overflow and Oracle communities, and speak at user groups and events. * Test new features early and turn what you hear from users into product input. * Join selected technical customer conversations as the trusted expert. **How your time is split** About half your time goes to YouTube and video, 30% to community and other content, 10% to product feedback and 10% to customer conversations. **What you bring** * **Oracle Fusion background:** hands-on experience with Fusion ERP, SCM or HCM data, including OTBI subject areas, BI Publisher, BICC extracts and Fusion security roles. * **Modern data stack fluency:** pipelines and incremental loads on at least one of Microsoft Fabric, Snowflake or Databricks, with strong SQL. * **BI fluency:** Power BI semantic models, Power Query, refresh and gateways, and dashboards business users act on. Tableau is a plus. * **Translation skill:** you explain Fusion concepts in the audience's terms, not in Oracle jargon. * **On-camera teaching:** clear spoken English, calm pacing, and you explain the why, not just the clicks. * **Shipping discipline:** a track record of publishing on a schedule (a channel, course or webinar series). * You might be a great fit if you are an Oracle Fusion technical or reporting consultant who has moved into Power BI, Fabric or data engineering, or an Oracle Analytics or OBIEE developer now building on Power BI, Snowflake or Databricks. **Nice to have** * Your own YouTube channel or Udemy course on Power BI, SQL or Oracle. * Microsoft Certified Trainer, Microsoft MVP, Databricks Certification, or Oracle ACE. * Basic video editing (Camtasia, Descript, Premiere or DaVinci Resolve). * YouTube SEO and analytics experience. * Developer relations, developer advocacy or technical training experience (helpful, not required). **Hiring process** * Portfolio review (existing videos, courses or talks). * Paid assignment: a short tutorial video that explains one Oracle Fusion concept for a data engineer or BI developer. * Technical interview * Live demo with the team. **Compensation** Competitive base salary plus a performance bonus. **How to apply** Send your resume and links to your videos, courses or talks to hiring@guidanz.com.

f42ebc148a310b3b.description:
Associate Product Manager (APM)
SBNRI · Product · [Gurgaon, in-office] · [0–2 years] · [Full-time]

About SBNRI
35 million NRIs are trying to manage their money from thousands of miles away, and most of them don't trust anyone enough to help. SBNRI is building the company that changes that. We help NRIs in 120+ countries invest and manage money in India: mutual funds, fixed deposits, taxation, compliance, and repatriation.
The role
You'll own real product problems end to end: figure out what's broken, work out why, ship the fix with Engineering and Design, and measure whether it worked. You'll report to the Head of Product and work closely with Engineering, Design, Growth, Operations, and leadership.
Problems like the ones you'll work on:
• Why does an NRI in Dubai start onboarding and not finish?
• What makes an investor redeem, and what could have kept them?
• Which manual workflows should AI be running instead of people?

What you'll do
• Define winning before you build: Every initiative starts with a success metric. If you can't say what "this worked" looks like in numbers, it isn't ready.
• Execution: Write clear requirements, drive delivery with Engineering and Design, clear blockers, and close the loop. A task is yours until the outcome is delivered, not until you hand it off.
• Analytics: Track funnels, adoption, and conversion. Judge features by whether they move the business, not by whether they shipped.
• Talk to users every week: Have direct conversations with NRIs across geographies. Dashboards and CS summaries don't replace them. Support tickets and payment failures are requirements we missed, and you'll help trace them to root cause.
• AI and automation: Use AI tools daily to research, prototype, and automate. If something is repetitive, your first question should be "why isn't this automated?"
• Experimentation: Frame hypotheses, define success metrics, and read results honestly, including when an experiment fails.

What we look for
You don't need PM experience. We look for evidence of how you think and build:
• A product project: a college project, app, website, or prototype you took from idea to something usable
• Analytical thinking: the ability to take apart a product, find a real user problem, and back your fix with reasoning or data
• AI fluency: practical use of AI tools to research, prototype, or automate something real
• Ownership: a clear example of something you drove to completion, especially when it got hard

How we work
Your work will be challenged, and not in quarterly reviews. It happens in the moment, by the person next to you. A design gets torn apart because an NRI in Dubai would find it confusing. A feature gets sent back because it solves our problem, not the user's. That isn't conflict; it's how craft works when people care.
We don't optimize for comfort. We optimize for the NRI in San Jose at 11pm, trying to figure out if their money in India is safe. That person deserves our best thinking, our fastest execution, and our most obsessive attention to detail.
If that standard feels like pressure, this isn't the right place. If it feels like the point, you'll do the best work of your life here.

Why SBNRI
• A small team, so your work ships and is visible to leadership from week one
• A rare domain: cross-border, regulated wealth for a global customer base
• A steep learning curve across product, data, compliance, and growth

How to apply
Email sanskriti@sbnri.com with the subject "Application for Associate Product Manager – SBNRI." Include:
• Your resume
• One link to something you've built or analysed. This could be a product teardown, prototype, project, or a short doc on a problem you'd fix in any app you use.
Applications without the link won't be reviewed.

f4dccfc674c8005c.description: ## **About Metaforms** Metaforms is a vertically integrated AI SaaS platform for market research agencies around the world. The platform helps agencies improve speed, consistency, and delivery quality across research workflows that have historically depended on repetitive manual effort and hard-to-scale specialist knowledge. The product surface is unusual. Surveys behave like programs, business workflows contain hidden operational nuance, and a small mistake can create real downstream cost for an agency and its clients. That means product thinking here is not about copying familiar SaaS patterns. It is about understanding how work is actually done, identifying where AI agents can reliably help, and shaping systems that feel intuitive to users while introducing genuinely new workflows underneath. ## **The Role** Metaforms is hiring a Senior Product Manager to define and ship new AI-native products and workflow experiences for research operations. This role sits at the intersection of user discovery, domain synthesis, product design, and engineering execution. The right person is comfortable going end to end, from interviewing users and subject matter experts, to identifying operational bottlenecks, to translating business needs into concrete product requirements, to partnering closely with engineering through delivery. This is a high-ownership role for someone who likes ambiguous spaces, can reason from first principles, and can build from zero rather than relying on existing category templates. ## **What You'll Own** ### **User Discovery and Problem Definition** - Conduct frequent user interviews with market research operators, project managers, programmers, and agency leaders to understand how work actually happens. - Turn messy qualitative input into clear product insights, problem statements, and opportunity areas. - Work closely with subject matter experts to separate surface requests from deeper workflow or systems problems. - Build conviction on where AI agents can remove manual effort, improve turnaround time, or increase quality without disrupting critical trust points. ### **Product Design and 0 to 1 Development** - Define new product concepts, workflow patterns, and operating models for AI-assisted research work. - Design familiar-feeling user journeys that introduce new capabilities without overwhelming users. - Write product requirements that are specific enough for engineering to execute, while preserving room for iteration where the solution space is still emerging. - Iterate rapidly on prototypes, internal feedback, and early customer usage to converge on products that are both useful and operationally viable. ### **Cross-Functional Execution** - Translate business requirements into clear engineering asks, including scope, constraints, acceptance criteria, and edge cases. - Partner tightly with engineering, design, operations, and domain experts throughout the build cycle. - Drive prioritization decisions by balancing customer value, technical feasibility, reliability risk, and speed. - Ensure the team is solving the right problem, not just shipping the fastest version of the first idea. ### **Product Quality and Adoption** - Define what good looks like for product outcomes, user trust, and workflow adoption. - Identify failure modes in user flows, handoffs, and agent behavior, especially in high-consequence operational steps. - Close the loop between shipped behavior, customer feedback, and roadmap decisions. - Own rollout, onboarding, and change-management plans with customer success and operators so new workflows land in real agency production including how we measure adoption and efficiency gains. ## **What We're Looking For** ### **Must Have** - Product management experience with a strong track record of shipping software products from concept to launch. - Demonstrated ability to operate in ambiguous, early-stage, or zero-to-one product environments. - Gone beyond prompting with AI. At work or on the side, you’ve built a prototype, automated a workflow, or shipped a feature using LLMs, APIs, or agents, and can speak to the trade-offs you ran into. - Strong user discovery skills, including conducting interviews, extracting patterns, and synthesizing findings into product direction. - Comfort working deeply with subject matter experts and operational stakeholders in domains that are initially unfamiliar. - Ability to translate business context and user pain points into clear requirements for engineering teams. - Strong product judgment across scope, workflow design, trade-offs, and iterative delivery. - Comfort owning the end-to-end journey of how a product should be defined, shaped, and built. - Excellent written and verbal communication, especially in cross-functional settings where clarity matters more than volume. - Comfort going deep enough with engineering to write requirements that can be executed without a translator, including constraints, edge cases, and failure modes. - Willingness to reason about AI/agent behavior in production: when to trust automation, when to require human review, and how quality/reliability show up for users. - Bias toward defining and tracking workflow outcomes (speed, quality, trust/adoption), not only shipped scope. - Direct, high-ownership communication under incomplete information clarity over polish, and willingness to call out when process or product direction is wrong. ## **How Success Looks** - Users say the product fits how their work actually happens, not how software teams assumed it happened. - Engineering has clear, high-signal product inputs and can move quickly without repeated ambiguity tax. - New workflows feel intuitive enough to adopt, while still delivering meaningful gains in speed, quality, or operational leverage. - Product decisions reflect a strong understanding of both customer outcomes and the realities of production systems. - Shipped workflows show measurable gains in turnaround, quality, or adoption, with clear failure modes understood and managed not just features launched. ## **Why Metaforms** - Work on AI products that operate in real production environments, not demos or feature theater. - Shape entirely new workflow categories instead of incrementally copying existing tools. - Join a team where product, engineering, and domain understanding are tightly coupled. - Operate with high ownership, fast iteration loops, and direct influence on what gets built.
